## (1) The failing line, re-run (CONFIRMED)

**The pin, re-derived.** The case is the describe 'the band reaches attractCm inclusive on a steep sloped route: an
off-axis point exactly 26 cm from P (N-s2c-2)'. The checker's own brute-force oracle (`probe/oracle.mjs`, plain
JavaScript, no kernel import) on the shore (1 000, 1 100)–(2 000, 3 500): u = (1 000, 2 400), |Δy| > |Δx|, so
`shallow` is false and the band walks rows of y — the other branch; the slide's clamp `lo = 26 · 2 600` puts P at
(1 010, 1 124) exactly; the strip (perpendicular distance ≤ 0.71 cm) within 26 cm of P, the nearest point left out,
holds **76** points, the last two by (d, y, x) **(1 000, 1 100)** and **(1 020, 1 148)**, both at d² = 676 (the second
10² + 24², off the route's axes); the nearest points beyond are (1 000, 1 099) and (1 020, 1 149) at d² = 725, both
inside the strip and inside the loop's rows (1 098 … 1 150), so only `d > ATTRACT_SQ` drops them; every nearer point is
within minEdge of the shore's end or of the foot (1 010, 1 125) ((1 020, 1 147) is 24.17 cm from the foot), the end
fails test (i), and the first qualifier is (1 020, 1 148): **77** candidates charged. The case asserts exactly these:
`band.length` 76, the tail, no point of rows 1 149, 1 098, 1 099, `W_PLACED 1020,1148`,
`insert.placementCandidates` 77, no halving, `slide 1020,1148`, the foot unmoved, `healthy` — the counts asserted as
round S2's cases assert theirs, through `warp` and on the band directly.

apart, red on the new case — "the `shallow` test inverted, or its other branch's axis swapped": the five axis swaps
are red on the new case and **green on round S2's cases**; the inverted test is green on the new case and **red on

S3" carries it (its figures 76 → 74 for R2attr, 0 points for the `e0` swap and 77 → 76 for W4e equal the checker's).

**The checker's own judgement of the inverted test (not the author's label).** The two branches describe one strip, so
on a sloped route they must return the same list. CONFIRMED by a differential probe (`probe/diff.ts`: a copy of lines
96 – 122 with the test made a parameter, first proved equal to the real function on every draw): 185 015 random sloped
routes (any slope, near-diagonal, 1 : 4 000, short; P on the route or a lattice point beside it), **0 differences** for
the test inverted, forced true and forced false. So Sinv is an equivalent on every sloped route and no sloped case can
kill it; what tells the branch's selection is an axis-aligned route, where the other branch divides by zero and
returns null. Horizontal routes: round S2's cases (Sinv, Sfalse red). Vertical routes: nothing — **Strue survives the
whole NEAR folder at full strength** (5 files, 82/82, B-FUZZ at 10⁴, seed −807604782, `mut/Strue-near.log`), and it is
not an equivalent: the checker's probe case on a vertical shore (`variants/vertical.ts`) is green on the code and red
under Strue. That is a new finding outside the row's stated promise (the row names a SLOPED route and accepts the axis
swap as the telling mutant); it is a missing hardening test on code that is right, so by the blocker rule it is note
**N-s3c-1**, not a failing line. The session may prefer to queue its one pin with the next kernel round.

A fresh seat of the lane read the finished chain (`chain.done` present, the chain's process gone, eight `.rc` files) and

earlier sittings' summary: `warp.ts` lines 1 – 200 (`onRoutePixel`, `hotPixelCandidates`, `placeOnRoute`), round S2's two
cases and the new case in `fixtures.test.ts`, the notes rows N-s2c-1, N-s2c-2, the builder's section and N-s3c-1, -2.
What it re-derived or re-read itself, each CONFIRMED:

* the pin's figures, by a second brute-force oracle of its own (`reentry/oracle2.mjs`, plain JavaScript): 76 band
  points, the tail (1 000, 1 100), (1 020, 1 148) at d² = 676, no point of row 1 149, none below row 1 100 — at 0.71 cm
  and at √½ cm alike; (1 020, 1 148) lies on the line exactly (20 · 12 − 48 · 5 = 0) and (1 020, 1 149) 5/13 = 0.38 cm off it,
  inside the strip, so only `d > ATTRACT_SQ` drops it;
* the mutant table, from the result files `mut/*.json` themselves (R2attr: three reds, the new case `expected 74 to be
  76`; the five steep-branch swaps: one red each, the new case only; Sinv: six reds, the new case green; Strue: 0 of 47
  red; `Ssteep-q+before`: 0 of 46 red; `R2attr+door`: `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'W_PLACED 1020,1148' ]`) and
  `mutate.py`'s edit texts;
* the equivalence of the inverted test on a sloped route, by reading the code: either branch walks the lattice points
  whose perpendicular distance from the line is at most `HOT_PIXEL_CM` (half-width `HOT_PIXEL_CM · len / |along|` along
  the walked axis is that strip), and `d ≤ ATTRACT_SQ` implies the walked range `e0 ± ATTRACT` on either axis — one set
  either way. On an axis-aligned route the other branch has `along` = 0 and `ratio` refuses: null. So the survivor
  Strue is a missing pin for a VERTICAL route on code that is right (N-s3c-1), outside the row's stated promise
  (a sloped route; "inverted, or its other branch's axis swapped") — a note, not a blocker. The seat agrees with the
  first sitting's classing after its own reading;
* sha256 of `warp.ts` `3845540c…7157b4` and of `fixtures.test.ts` `a26c3236…d832d1` (unchanged since the first sitting,
